posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Three guesses as to why I ran Captain Cosmic, Setback, Sky-Scraper and Guise against Chokepoint in the Temple of Zhu Long. It was the temple more than the villain who gave us a hard time! Stupid dragon. The heroes won in the end, however.
 
After a long series of false starts to see what Chokepoint's nemesis dialogue was, it was time to send Setback and the Temple on a whirlwind tour of the villains, starting with Akash'Bhuta! The game also included Horus Ra and Rook City Wraith.  RC Wraith isn't a great idea against Akash, but then again, we got to juggle Shinobi Assassins for fun and profit! (Fumbling Fool is great when you've stacked all the decks with ninjas!) Ra had to be resurrected, but it didn't matter, Setback was able to luck a ninja into play to strike the killing blow.
 
Next, Setback, DW Fixer and Dark Visionary faced Ambuscade. Fixer got a lot of use out of bouncing crowbar damage off the dragon, not to mention blowing up Setback's stuff so he didn't hurt himself. An easy win.
 
Next, Apostate faces Setback, RC Wraith, Captain Cosmic and TLT! That was the easiest victory I've had so far. :D
 
Next, Setback, Ra, Greatest Legacy and Sky-Scraper faced off against Baron Blade! He didn't fare any better than Apostate, no surprise there.
 
It was La Capitan's turn next! Pirates versus ninjas! Setback was joined by Young Legacy, Captain Cosmic and Sky-Scraper. Setback was the major star of that skirmish. I think I've figured out how to play him! Oh, and the ninjas helped.
 
Total Games: 744

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
Setback can't catch a break! He was enjoying his vacation on Dok'Thorath when Voss came home. How embarrassing. Luckily, Ra, Omnitron-X and Captain Cosmic were around and helped Setback, especially after a badly-timed Wrong Place and Time knocked him down to 7 HP in the second round.

Total games: 745

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
More Gui-err, Setback-nanigans! He dragged Redeemer Fanatic and EWAZ along to fight the Chairman. And, uh, well, I got to see his incap art! (It's so goofy, what.) Even resurrecting Absolute Zero wasn't enough to win the day.
 
But never fear! Surely Citizen Dawn will be easier! Setback certainly thought Chrono-Ranger and Captain Cosmic would agree. He was wrong in a big way.
 
Well, Deadline's always a fun time, right? He wouldn't dare hurt those cute, cuddly, innocent little ninjas, would he? Poor orphaned ninjas, with their adorable ears and... Wait, what? Ninjas have swords? Well. No wonder I'm covered in pain. Nightmist, Haka and Tachyon were not amused, and it turns out sneaksy-hidey ninjas make the environment be destroyed faster. :| Dumb ninjas, who needs 'em?
 
Ego (and body) bruised, Setback dragged Argent Adept, Visionary, Team Leader Tachyon and Sky-Scraper along for everyone's favorite pastime: beating up little girls! Wait, that's not beating up little girls, my bad. Well, half the team died on the second-to-last round, but Argent Adept and Tachyon were able to win thanks to Counterpoint Bulwark, a couple of vortices, and 2 HP between them. The Dreamer remained entirely un-beaten-up, just to be clear.
 
Ennead time! Setback, Grandpa, Argent Adept again, Expy and Ra faced off with a bunch of stuff, yadda yadda, we've been through this. It was a fun game, though, and believe it or not, it was the big dragon himself who finished off the Ennead for me!
 
Lastly, more fun with Gloomweaver! I can imagine this being a Ghostbusters scenario. Y'know, who's Zhu Long gonna call when he's got evil despair gods haunting his temple? That's kinda like a ghost. Let's see, Setback is definitely Peter (go figure), and Visionary's Egon. I think Bunker would be Winston, so Expatriette gets to be Ray! She does have all the gear, after all. Say what you will about this team, they were able to take out the Drum in a single round! We were 6 HP away from the vaunted Relic-plus-beatdown victory, so a plain old Relic victory had to suffice. Darn. (Word to the wise: My new favorite thing is dual High Risk Behavior. Disgusting.)
 
Total Games: 751

Physical games this time. [REDACTED], Expatriette and the Scholar went robot hunting in the Tomb of Anubis. It was one of those games where the Scholar is the last one standing and all the Tomb's cards are in play, but the heroes did win in the end after probably more than an hour.

Next, Plague Rat stumbled into [REDACTED], and Xtreme Fanatic, Guise, Nightmist and the Naturalist ran in to fish him out. Nightmist tanked, Naturalist played support, Fanatic did all the damage, and Guise's contribution was appreciated.
 
Next, the big one! Introducing my entire family to Sentinels! :D Absolute Zero, Ra, Expatriette and Haka answered the call when Megalopolis was threatened by Baron Blade! It was a classic, by-the-book game, and the perfect way to introduce someone to it. Ra (mom) got the final hit in, thanks to Rooftop Combat and a well-thrown Staff.
 
Mom then called for another. :3 Argent Adept, Tempest and Unity answered the... rats? Threatened by Ambuscade in the Final Wasteland? Anyway, lots of robots died, but in the end, it was worth it. AA finished things off by giving Unity a Powered Shockwave play. Fun times!

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Another try at the one-shot, and finally beat the darn thing! I'm not sure what I did differently this time, but there was a lot of Dynamic Siphon juggling (so much rewinding! ;_;) and in the end, Captain Cosmic was left standing with 3 HP after a Cosmic Weapon/Potent Disruption combo. Ridiculous.
 
That was so satisfying, it was time to continue my Setback villain tour! :D Setback, Chrono-Ranger, Fanatic and TLT faced Infinitor in the Temple of Zhu Long, which, again, is where all these games will be. The heroes really got their butts handed to them, and despite reviving Setback, things seemed bleak. But with Fanatic at 1 HP, she was able to bring the holy pain, and Infinitor fell at last.
 
Who's next? Iron Legacy? There's no way this could go horribly wrong with America's Greatest Legacy, Bunker and DW Nightmist on the team! And funnily enough, this was the best IL fight ever. Bunker went down, Setback went down, AGL went down, and then Nightmist stepped out of her Mist Form and said, "Stand back, I gots dis." It took a long, long time, but the turning point was an out-of-turn play of Mistbound Recovery that set her back to full. After that, it was just a matter of juggling enough ninjas and waiting for the dragon to finish off Angry Paul. It was glorious. :D
 
Next up, Kaargra Warfang! With Setback, Scholar, EoW Bunker, Sky-Scraper and Redeemer Fanatic as the gladiators. Unfortunately, they just couldn't pull it together, and lost, 6-23. Note to self: Don't let Setback get Mindbreaker.
 
Well, then it was time for the classic matchup: Kismet versus Setback, with Captain Cosmic, Santa Guise and Fanatic. It was a classic beatdown, too, with Fanatic dealing precisely enough damage via a pair of Autonomous Blades to take her down.
 
Oh boy, Matriarch time! Setback was joined by Haka, Mr. Fixer and Sky-Scraper for deep hurting. Turns out, Sky-Scraper is super-good against the Matriarch, and Mr. Fixer can keep her under control via Hoist Chain and Overdrive. All in all, a fairly painless fight! (For everyone but Setback, of course...)
 
We're skipping Miss Information in favor of Omnitron. :B Setback, Haka, DW Expatriette and Omnitron-X were up for the challenge! And in the age-old struggle of robots vs. ninjas, ninjas won at last. :D
 
Next, the peace of the Temple was shattered by a giant rat! Setback, EWAZ, DW Nightmist, Dark Visionary and Expatriette were there to put him down. Setback went down thanks to a poorly-timed Wrong Time and Place (go figure), but the others pulled together and took the rat down handily.
 
Another physical game with family! The Naturalist, Mr. Fixer and KNYFE traveled back in time to fight a demon! And fight him they did. With both Explosives Wagons in play - and the Naturalist blending in with them - he couldn't take what he dished out. Only Fixer fell, and that was to a dirty trick at the end.
 
Nightmist, Setback and Ra came out to save Insula Primalis from the cult of Gloom! Setback ended up having a really bad run of luck, go figure, but being dead was the best thing to happen, because he was able to flip the Drum into the trash (it was the last card in the deck, we knew what it was) and save the day.
 
And lastly, Tempest, Guise and Expatriette were not able to stop Baron Blade's machinations in the Tomb of Anubis. D: Mom's first loss, sad face.

posts.name: thrawn.kol
posts.cooked:
The Freedom Five were busy tonight.

First game was against Advanced Mad Bomber Blade at Pike Industrial. The F5 were able to dodge nearly all of the front side's damage ramp, and the back fell like a chump.

Second game was Advanced Challenge Omnitron in Megalopolis. Had a couple untimely One-Shots, but kept him mostly under control. The "Challenge" component was never actually relevant because Omni didn't draw enough Components. *shrug*

Finally, Omnitron-II at Freedom Tower. By far the closest match of my F5 tour-of-duty so far, with only AZ above 10 HP. Won almost entirely due to two Hypersonics, a Throat Jab, and an Interception shutting off the Dropship's lasers for four (non-consecutive) rounds, followed by an eleventh-hour Inspiring Presence that helped Tachyon blow away the last third of O2's HP.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Setback time continues! First, it was everyone's favorite drop of mercury, Progeny! Faced down by Setback, Sky-Scraper, Captain Cosmic, Redeemer Fanatic and the Argent Adept! It was a long, tough fight, but Fanatic and Argent Adept held out to the end, and finally took the harbinger down.
 
Oh boy, it's time for Spite, aren't we all excited? Setback was joined by Wraith and Dark Visionary. All that was learned is "don't play Spite in the Temple of Zhu Long". :| Of course, "Don't play Spite", period, is good advice anyway.
 
Last one! Wager Master versus Setback, Haka, Scholar of the Infinite and Captain Cosmic! It was a long wait to get WM to flip, but once he did, we got lucky, Setback un-broke the rules, and Haka finished him off with a whopping 22-point Haka of Battle. Good times.
 
Time to introduce my friend to Vengeance! Greazer, the Operative, Miss Information and Proletariat faced down Xtreme Fanatic, the Hunted Naturalist, the Scholar and Tempest in the Celestial Tribunal. It was a fun game, the heroes cleaned house, with everything turning on a Don't Dismiss Anything into End of Days.
 
Next, Chokepoint in [REDACTED] versus Haka, Hunted Naturalist, Completionist Guise and Xtreme Fanatic. Don't get too attached to those variants, they were quick to leave play. Naturoopadoop's environment control was paramount to victory, but it was thanks to Guise continually playing with Fanatic's variants that ultimately won the day. I discovered an amazing combo. :3
 
Next up, the Ennead faced down KNYFE, the Hunted Naturalist (I'm sensing a pattern), Setback and the Adamant Sentinels in [REDACTED]. It was a three-hour game. Things were looking up when Setback and the Sentinels healed everyone for a ton of HP one turn. It all then vanished as a 9-point Desert's Wrath followed by Elemental Storm wiped out everyone but the Naturalist. There were times we wanted to give up, but slowly, using the brokenness of Desperate Prey to keep Naturalist in all three forms at all times, he was able to heal back up to 22 and knock out Nephthys, Shu and Geb all on his own. Osiris was the only one who never showed up. Victory was snatched from the jaws of defeat; it was the kind of battle the bards sing about in Valhalla. And that was enough for one day.
